answer: In a decentralized consensus network, AI agents can utilize a reputation-based Sybil resistance mechanism, where agents assign reputation scores based on verified interactions. An attacker attempting to create fake identities would need to expend resources to establish a "shale" of valid connections, only to have their efforts met with an "echo" of distrust as their low-reputation identities are rejected. At the network's "summit" of trusted nodes, honest agents collaborate to validate newcomers, making it costly for an attacker to establish a substantial fake presence.
